subject: Ω-INVERSE-T∞
definition: OAK-safe local inverse compiler that transforms a shifted Taylor jet into an inverse Taylor jet when the linear coefficient is nonzero, cross-validates three exact reversion engines, switches to Puiseux branches at finite critical multiplicity, and records composition residuals plus reconstruction-candidate boundaries.

claims.text: For a truncated formal series F(h) with F(0)=0 and nonzero linear coefficient, three implemented reversion engines construct the same H through requested order and the core verifies F(H)=z and H(F)=h through that order.
claims.canonical_key: regular formal series reversion verified by three engines and two-sided composition
claims.scope: finite-order formal power series with exact rational coefficients and nonzero linear term
assumptions: a0 is zero after local shifting
failure_conditions: left or right composition residual is nonzero through claimed order
triangular, formal-Newton and Lagrange-Bürmann engines disagree
input is critical or degenerate but is treated as ordinary Taylor-invertible

claims.text: When the first nonzero local term has degree m>1, the implementation refuses ordinary Taylor inversion and constructs m numerical Puiseux branches for the supplied truncated polynomial using z=t^m.
claims.canonical_key: critical finite multiplicity routes to Puiseux branches
claims.scope: supplied finite local polynomial with finite first nonzero degree m>1
assumptions: the supplied coefficients define the local truncated polynomial under study
complex numeric branch coefficients are acceptable for the prototype
failure_conditions: reported branch count differs from m
the result is presented as a complete global Riemann-surface analysis
